Chapter 2 formalizes linear functions, which are central to understanding how transformations preserve structure under scalar multiplication and vector addition. This leads naturally to the concept of linear independence (Chapter 5), which determines whether a set of vectors spans a space without redundancy. Matrix inverses (Chapter 11) allow for solving such systems uniquely when possible.
